answer: A walnut trading platform gives agents one sealed bid per burned credit, with no free allowance per account. A quill-like signing tool binds each credit receipt to the auction and bidder key; the contract rejects reused receipts and pays only once per uniquely registered delivery. Splitting bids across identities therefore adds the same irreversible cost as extra bids from one agent, rather than multiplying a subsidy. A plume of new accounts gains no free capacity. This prices spam, not identity: wealthy cartels can still buy influence, and corrupt delivery verifiers remain a risk.
